title: situation.muscogee_treaty.title
railroad: the nation's own treaty of 10 July with the Confederacy, its government's act (0070); a nation's council is not modelled, so its treaty comes on its date once the Confederacy's act is in place, independent of either principal's choices

citations.at: treaty with the Creek Nation, 10 July 1861: signatures p. 301 (Moty Kinniard, Principal Chief; Icho Hacho, Principal Chief Upper Creeks); the General Council's ratification of 20 July, p. 302 ("Motey Kinnaird, Principal Chief, Icho Hacho, First Chief of the Upper Creeks"); Opothleyahola appears nowhere among the signers, pp. 301 to 303

notes.route|confederate_protection_act: The treaty follows only the Confederate Congress's act of 21 May, a dated event under the interim Confederate rule (0046), never a principal's option or goal, nor a flag a principal's choice set or cleared (0070, 0071). The nation answers what happened. Its treaty does not read indian_territory_posts_given_up, which follows the president's call, and must not.
notes.item: The commissioners' treaty of 10 July. Its signers are taken from the printed signatures (CSA-STAT p. 301). Opothleyahola's absence is stated, so the nation's division is not hidden (risk: agency). It is the nation's own act (0070).
